correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the exact published formula, removes mass scaling, and differentiates its logarithm. The derived auxiliary function H has derivative \(H'(p)=-1/(p-1)+p[\psi_1(p-1/2)-\psi_1(p)]\). The trigamma integral and the strict AM-GM bound imply \(H'(p)<0\) for every \(p>1\). Since \(H(p)\to+\infty\) at \(1^+\) and \(H(3/2)=4\log2-3<0\), exactly one zero exists; its sign controls the derivative of the threshold. Numerical root finding is not used for the global proof.

value.rationale: The curve is a sharp spectral-collapse threshold. After natural mass normalization, proving that it has exactly one maximizer identifies a unique exponent of greatest threshold resistance and excludes secondary extrema globally. This rigorously resolves a structural feature that the source presents only numerically; it is a motivated theorem about the sharp constant itself, not a routine substitution or arbitrary parameter slice.
